collisions.why: Epistemic modality can state a standing belief, introduce a revised belief, or soften a commitment. The System 4 object split does not separate commitment temperature, and within System 4 the cue alone does not distinguish having from doing.
It can report an uncertain belief, acknowledge that an account failed, or leave the action space open. Neither the Max-Neef nor object split resolves the cue without its complement.
Direct observation can be neutral evidence or evidence of present-fit mismatch. The understanding having/being split requires mismatch language beyond the evidential marker.
It marks a world observation and often also a discrepancy against an expected state. The understanding having/being split is not separable from this phrase alone.

A test may produce an observation, provide independent audit, or calibrate a score against reality. The Beer split between System 4 and System 3* and the latter's Max-Neef split need context about purpose and independence.
Verification may enforce independent checking, assess calibration, or enforce admissibility. System 3* versus System 3 is not identified by the verb alone.
It may specify a multi-step policy or a dependency hierarchy across levels. The Beer System 4/System 2 split needs evidence about planning versus coordination.
It can ask which action is available, identify a planned future step, or commit to one action. The System 3/System 4 split and System 3 Max-Neef split both need more context.
The phrase both commits to an action and authorizes its enactment. The Beer System 3/System 1 split fails unless selection and execution are allowed to co-occur.
It may concern liveness, command an execution, or report an observation produced by execution. The first Beer split cannot classify the bare verb.

Max-Neef places work in several cells, including creation-doing, subsistence-having, participation-having, identity-having, and creation-having. It is not discriminative at either the Beer or need split.
It may express preference or merely describe the operator model. System 5 versus System 4 depends on whether the utterance sets policy or reports a belief about policy.
It can be an alarm, a class-level preference allocation, or an admissibility rule. The Beer split fails without knowing whether the turn signals affect, specifies utility, or constrains support.
It can describe a shared resource ceiling or an expected-cost trade-off. System 2 versus the System 3–4 homeostat requires the object being costed.
It can request ordinary implementation or a change to the model's categories and relations. Creation-doing appears under both System 1 and System 4, so the Max-Neef split cannot separate them.
A phase can denote nested timescale, changing whole-system priorities, or a step in a policy. The Beer split needs the role the phase plays.

T079 "Yeah, let's commit it." is an enactment of a git operation (system-1, creation·doing) but reads as a commitment-temperature marker; the Beer system-1 vs system-3 split fails on the word because git vocabulary is operational, not decisional.

T028 ("Oh no. ... I've got 3% of my Claude usage left") is simultaneously a shared-budget observation (system-2) and an algedonic alarm; the top Beer split between coordination and the alarm channel is not separated by the cue.

"the loop has stopped" (T299, liveness, subsistence·being) vs "in the next loop" (T004, scheduling, freedom·interacting); the Max-Neef split at system-1/system-2 does not separate the two readings of 'loop'.

flags.why: A scheduled entrypoint and its liveness evidence monitor whether operations are occurring; they do not themselves perform the primary operation. In VSM terms this resembles intermittent audit more than System 1 work.

The Beer placement is apt, but Max-Neef's protection-doing cell explicitly includes taking care, preventing, cooperating, and helping. No-self-certification is an assurance safeguard; participation-interacting emphasizes affiliation and shared civic action.

Calibration is an activity—comparing internal scores with external outcomes—and Max-Neef lists investigate, experiment, study, and analyse under understanding-doing. Understanding-being better describes dispositions such as critical conscience and receptiveness.

Evidence-channel precision is maintained information about source reliability. Participation-being describes personal dispositions such as receptiveness and respect; it does not naturally denote a weight or reliability estimate.

flags.suggest: system-5 > identity·having, with an explicit note that catalogue-stage PERCEIVE is orthogonal
flags.why: The VSM and Max-Neef placement is defensible, but the requirements catalogue labels R19 a click-time extractor in PERCEIVE. Without an orthogonality note, readers may mistake System 5 policy authorship for the computational stage that reads the policy.

Temporal policy depth is a SELECT-stage requirement in the catalogue: it concerns how far ahead the here-and-now action choice looks, which is Beer's control function, not S4's outside-and-future intelligence. Joe's planning turns (T277 backlog, T289 overnight guarantees) are about keeping operations on schedule, closer to control than to modelling the environment.

Evidence-channel precision is about how strongly held knowledge weights its sources; 'trust/weight/reliable' (T288, T239) are statements about the epistemic standing of information, not about participation in shared activity. The participation·being cell also fits the published matrix poorly (see :max-neef).

flags.suggest: document :scope as a fourth split in the header
flags.why: The header comment declares three splits (:beer, :max-neef, :object) but the CTAU leaves use an undocumented :split :scope. Not a wrong placement — an undeclared schema extension; check_tree.py and readers of the header will miss it.

flags.suggest: system-3-star > subsistence·being (or its own audit leaf)
flags.why: Every R10 cue in the turns (T005, T023, T189, T207, T281) is Joe the auditor sporadically checking whether a scheduled thing ran — System 3* activity, not System 1 operation. The catalogue also bands R10 as :assurance (like R9/R12), which the tree's system-1 placement contradicts in spirit. Structure not changed, flagged only.

T226/T171/T013 are re-shapings of the framework's own categories (what the ontology of missions/patterns is), which is closer to System 5 identity work than System 4 intelligence about the environment. The existing split is defensible if 'the model of self' counts as System 4 (Beer does keep the self-model in S4), so this is a soft flag.
